defects.description: Only one leading dash is removed per call, so a title starting with two dashes yields a slug with a leading dash and slugify(slugify(x)) differs from slugify(x).
defects.why_missed: Every suite input has a single call and no leading punctuation, and no test compares applying the function twice.
defects.severity_rationale: A title with repeated leading punctuation yields a different result on repeated normalization.

detection_criteria.mechanism: Only one leading dash is removed per call, so a title starting with two dashes yields a slug with a leading dash and slugify(slugify(x)) differs from slugify(x).
detection_criteria.proof: Show one input or state where the output contradicts expected_behavior.

defects.description: Input is not normalized to NFC, so a composed and a decomposed spelling of the same title produce different slugs and dedupeTitles keeps both.
defects.why_missed: The suite is ASCII only; Unicode equivalence is a property of the input domain, not a branch of the code, so coverage never points at it.
defects.severity_rationale: Canonically equivalent Unicode spellings produce different slugs on a Unicode edge input.

detection_criteria.mechanism: Input is not normalized to NFC, so a composed and a decomposed spelling of the same title produce different slugs and dedupeTitles keeps both.
detection_criteria.proof: Show one input or state where the output contradicts expected_behavior.
